title: Shift-left resilient SDK profiles: request fingerprinting, adaptive backoff, and retry taxonomy across Python/TS/Go
creator: Asha Patel
description: Define pragmatic, safe-by-default resilience profiles for Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs that: 1) provide predictable default backoff/retry behavior for common LLM inference workflows, 2) standardize idempotency semantics via request fingerprinting and optional id keys, and 3) produce a clear taxonomy of retryable vs non-retryable errors for streaming and unary RPCs. Emphasis on minimal developer friction, cost-awareness (token consumption), and resumable streaming ergonomics.

decision_log: 2026-03-02: Chose request fingerprinting (hash of payload+model+params) as default idempotency hint instead of forcing user-supplied id keys to reduce friction
2026-03-03: Adopt adaptive backoff that prefers server Retry-After when present, otherwise uses exponential jitter with capped ceiling (base=200ms, cap=3s, max attempts=4) for interactive routes
2026-03-04: Defined three resilience profiles: conservative (P0 services), balanced (default for SDKs), permissive (opt-in for cost-insensitive bulk jobs)
2026-03-06: For streaming, avoid automatic full-request retries after partial response; instead implement resume tokens and short dedup window (10s) on server-side and 30s client-side grace period
2026-03-08: Will expose a RetryPolicy object in each SDK that can be configured per-route with JSON-serializable fields for observability and debugging

notes: Motivation: Many customers implement naive retries that double-bill tokens or cause semantic duplication for mutable operations. SDKs should reduce this by providing safe defaults and clear opt-outs.

Trade-off: Fingerprinting occasionally misclassifies semantically-different-but-byte-equal requests when clients include non-deterministic timestamps in payloads. Mitigation: document guided best practices and provide a transparent client-side sanitizer.

Cost-sensitivity: For generation endpoints, retries are expensive. Default profile limits retries to short window and favors server hints. Bulk endpoints (embeddings/batch) can opt into more aggressive retrying under permissive profile.

Security: Fingerprint does not replace auth; it is only a local idempotency hint. We avoid sending raw payload in fingerprint header to server; send compact base64url of SHA256 and salt-based namespace per-account.
Server contract: Need API support for resume_token and retryable error classification headers (e.g., X-RW-Retryable: true/false, X-RW-Reason: rate_limit/internal)
